title: leucothoe marginata
intro: Leucothoe marginata, commonly known as the Variegated Doghobble, is a species of flowering plant in the family Ericaceae. It is a shrub native to the southeastern United States, known for its beautiful white and green variegated leaves and its ability to provide shade and attract wildlife. Leucothoe marginata has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antiviral properties, which may help to soothe skin irritations, reduce fever, and combat infections. The bioactive constituents of Leucothoe marginata include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and tannins, which contribute to its therapeutic actions of anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial effects.
